clips.send: In 1850, getting from New York to San Francisco took months. By 1920 you could cross the country by train in under a week, phone your cousin, drive a Model T — even fly. In just 70 years the United States went from a nation of farms to the world’s biggest industrial power, and millions of immigrants did much of the work. How did it happen so fast?
